results.content:
I had a very poor experience with MyClaw.  
The platform encourages you to purchase a subscription first, giving the impression that you’ll be able to use the system immediately. However, after subscribing, you are then required to purchase additional credits just to actually use the AI. This was not made clear upfront and feels extremely misleading.  
On top of that, the platform itself is unstable:  
Sessions crash or freeze  
Messages disappear without being processed  
Generated outputs are difficult or impossible to access (e.g. broken links)  
Core features such as media handling and file delivery do not work reliably [...] I spent a significant amount of time trying to get basic functionality working and ultimately achieved very little. What should have been a straightforward workflow turned into constant troubleshooting.  
When I contacted support, the response was that the platform is going through “growing pains.” That may be the case, but customers should not be paying for a product that is not yet functioning properly or transparently priced.  
In its current state, I cannot recommend this platform. It feels unfinished, unreliable, and poorly communicated in terms of actual costs and capabilities. [...] It's a scam, paid 120 USD for the subscription and tokens, wasted more than 3 hours trying to make it work, and it was impossible. Crashes every 5 minutes, buggy UI, forced restarts. It just does not work. Please don't throw your money away

System is experimenting with people’s money, the founder of openclaw openly admitted losing so much money on the project, and i think they are trying to recover it from our pockets, it doesn’t work, you save a skill.md file and it forgets it, and burns through tokens seriously in 3 days sometimes i spent 200 usd on tokens, crazy setup cheaper to hire real people.

The community is growing too. r/myclaw is 9 months old and is already a Top 100 AI & Machine Learning community on Reddit. MyClaw ran an AMA there on Nov 20 with founders, the tech lead and PMs, asking whether AI teams can replace a whole department.

A real-world example of the idea came on Saturday, Nov 21. Builder Cwyn said their AI team merged 23 pull requests in one day. They used a build queue on two Mac minis and up to 877 tests on every change. An AI audit caught a broken buy button before any customer did.

Reaction so far is mixed. Many posters say they want fewer tools competing for attention and a teammate that understands the outcome. One user said agents can feel like a day of fighting with nothing useful done. At least one promoting post was marked as a paid partnership. [...] Key numbers:
- Harnesses: Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, Pi, OpenClaw

- Plans: $19, $39 and $79 per month

MyClaw just launched MyClaw 3.0, a 24/7 AI agent team. Here's what you need to know.

The pitch is raised AI teammates with tools built in, not a blank agent you babysit. The launch post went up Nov 18 and has 2.1M views. Setup is ready in about 30 seconds.

You can run an agent on any harness: Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, Pi or OpenClaw, all with shared context. It plugs into 5,000+ live data sources, so you don't hunt for APIs. You can reach it from the browser, Slack, Teams, Telegram or WhatsApp.

Each teammate runs on a cloud supercomputer. Pricing on the official page is Lite at $19/mo, Pro at $39/mo and Max at $79/mo. Model usage is charged separately.

results.content:
## Critical analysis

MyClaw 3.0 addresses a real pain point. Setting up an agent with the right tools, data access and a machine that stays on is still fiddly, and a “pick a role, pick an engine” product is a sensible answer. Letting customers switch harnesses as the agent landscape changes week to week is a genuine differentiator. [...] The open questions are about substance. The launch materials give no benchmarks, customer results or detail on how shared memory works across very different harnesses. The “5,000+ live data sources” figure is not broken down publicly. The credit system makes it hard to compare costs with running the same agents yourself. And the unusual volume of templated praise on X is a reason to wait for independent hands-on reviews before drawing conclusions about quality.

## What’s still open [...] ## Pros and cons

### For users

- Pro: Ready-made roles and chat apps you already use lower the barrier to having an assistant that works in the background.
- Con: Credits make costs hard to predict, and agents that act in your accounts need careful permissions.

### For developers

- Pro: Switching between harnesses such as Claude Code, Codex and OpenClaw with shared context avoids lock-in to one agent framework.
- Con: A hosted layer on top of open-source agents adds another dependency, and how well context really transfers between harnesses is not documented in detail.
